content: MTCH1, also known as mitochondrial carrier homolog 1 or presenilin 1-associated protein (PSAP), is a protein encoded by the MTCH1 gene located on chromosome 6 in humans. This protein is proapoptotic in nature and may play a role in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). The protein encoded by the MTCH1 gene is named for its structural similarity to members of the mitochondrial carrier protein family. The MTCH1 gene consists of 12 exons and produces four distinct isoforms. These isoforms are generated through alternative splicing of exon 8 and the use of two potential start codons, which result in the deletion of 17 amino acid residues in the hydrophilic loop between two transmembrane domains in some isoforms. Despite differences in sequence and length, all four isoforms share a similar topological structure. This structure includes six transmembrane domains, one of which is responsible for targeting the protein to the outer mitochondrial membrane (OMM), and two N-terminal apoptotic domains. Consequently, all isoforms retain these apoptotic domains and mitochondrial localization, both of which are essential for the protein’s proapoptotic function. MTCH1 is a proapoptotic protein that localizes to the OMM and induces apoptosis independently of the proapoptotic proteins BAX and BAK. One proposed mechanism suggests that MTCH1 interacts with the mitochondrial permeability transition pore (MPTP) complex, leading to depolarization of the mitochondrial membrane, release of cytochrome c, and activation of caspase-3. The expression of MTCH1 has been observed in 16 different tissue types, suggesting that it may serve a general housekeeping function. MTCH1 may be associated with Alzheimer’s disease and other neurodegenerative and neuroinflammatory conditions due to its close interaction with presenilin. However, further research is needed to confirm its clinical relevance and involvement in these diseases. MTCH1 has been shown to interact with presenilin 1 (PS1).
